cues: Some far messengers cross deserts and canoes
But there was one more kind of crossing And it is the longest of them all
No desert on earth is as wide
The crossing of time
Between a grandmother and her great-grandchildren
Lies a gap that has swallowed more human knowledge
Than every desert and every ocean combined
When someone goes uncrossed
They take the whole library of themselves with them
And no caravan can go there to bring it back
So every people raise messengers for that crossing too
The ones who watched the weather and read the clouds across years
Until she could tell the people what was coming
The seed keeper who bred the hardy forward
Generation upon generation The one who kept the count of the years
The song holder who carried the whole library of a people Inside his own memory
Let me tell you about some of them In West Africa there were families whose calling held
For 700 years and more Was to be the living memory of the people
They carried the family lines, histories, the laws, and the songs
Not as a summary but whole
Held in the trained mind and given by the trained voice
At many great occasions it was a woman's voice that carried them
It was said that When one of the old keepers is gone
A whole library burns They trained for decades
Because a history told wrong could break a people apart
And underneath it all was the same calm body
Every far messenger depends on The same stillness that found the seep in the sand
Found the verse in the memory It was always one skill
In Australia a song can carry a person
Across thousands of kilometers of desert The song is the country itself In order This rock Then the water hole
Then the place where the ridge turns And you go left not right
When the song reaches the edge of one people's country
It is handed on In another language and carried further
So somewhere in the middle There is a person singing a stretch of country They will never walk
Getting it exactly right for thousands of years
For someone they will never meet It is one of the largest memory systems human beings have ever built
And it ran on nothing but voices and obligation and honor
In 1865 the Lithuanian people were forbidden to print books in their own alphabet
The ban lasted 40 years So ordinary people
Farmers mostly Carried books in on foot Through the forest at night Across the border
Risking prison and exile
Each one walked one stretch And handed the books on They were called
Knygnešiai The book carriers
And that word exists In no other language
Every year on March 16 Lithuania still honors them Because of them
A people kept its language And the language kept the people
It is how they remember their songs Their dances
And their ceremonies and rituals still
In one story An old carrier remembers his grandmother
Who could not read But keeping those books hidden for 30 years
When he asked her what was in them She said
Us, we are in them Halfway around the world
In the mountains of Mindanao in the Philippines
The Blaan people kept rice Not one kind
But more than a hundred types Each with its own name
Its own feel And its own season
Farmers there could still name One hundred and eighty
One hundred and eight kinds When people went looking for the seed
They found only forty-six The seed was not lost first The practice was
The names stopped being said The names stopped being said out loud
Here is what these keepers prove
The runner crosses space And the hands The knowing
And hands the knowing To someone who he can see
The keeper of memory
And hands it to people She will never see
The unborn The great-grandchildren Of the great-grandchildren
She runs a relay In which the next runner Has not been born yet
And she runs it anyway Her whole life long
Because she knows She knows the unborn are real
Mostly the knowledge is still here
What went is the carrying
If the carrying stops for one generation It can still be picked up
Not two That is the work Of the far messenger Of time
To carry something precious enough That the next person Can take it And you are one
Every family holds something That lives only one person Every song A recipe A story
A way of doing things This week
Sit with the oldest person you know Ask the questions You never have asked
And record the answer Keep it in two places
Then say the names out loud So the young ones learn them
You carried it to a place There was somebody there
They carried on
